## JSON in C#

**`System.Text.Json`** is the BCL stack for JSON. This chapter uses **`JsonSerializer`** on **`Dictionary<string, object>`** and **`JsonDocument`** so solutions compile cleanly in single-file `Program.cs` top-level programs (no file-scoped type ordering surprises).

exercises.title: Serialize a struct
exercises.description: Build a JSON object for `Name=Alice`, `Age=30` and print it with stable key order (`Name` then `Age`).
hints: `Dictionary<string, object>` preserves insertion order on modern .NET

exercises.title: Deserialize JSON
exercises.description: Parse `{"Name":"Bob","Age":25}` and print `Bob 25` on one line.

exercises.title: Property names
hints: Dictionary keys are the JSON keys verbatim

exercises.title: Omit nulls
exercises.description: Serialize only `Server` with value `api.example.com` (capital `S`), omitting unset fields.

exercises.title: Round trip
exercises.description: Serialize a product `{id:1,name:Laptop,price:999.99}` camelCase, deserialize, and print two lines with the Go-style brace formatting.

exercises.title: Nested structs
exercises.description: Serialize nested `User` with PascalCase keys matching the checker output.

exercises.title: Encode a slice
exercises.description: Serialize a JSON array with two people objects.
hints: `List<Dictionary<string, object>>` serializes to a JSON array

exercises.title: Deferred nested JSON
exercises.description: Parse nested JSON, print `level`, then print the nested `data` object using `GetRawText()` to preserve key order.
hints: `GetRawText()` preserves the nested fragment from the source text

exercises.title: Decode an array
exercises.description: Parse a JSON array of people and print `Name Age` per line.
